title: Newton's dice bet: one six from 6, or three from 18?
description:
In 1693 Samuel Pepys asked Isaac Newton which is likelier: at least one six from 6 dice, two from 12, or three from 18. Pepys thought 18 dice were best; Newton showed the opposite. With 6 dice you only lose if all six miss, (5/6)^6 = 33%, so you win 67%. With 18 dice you lose on zero, one or two sixes, 40% together, so you win only 60% (12 dice: 62%). Same one six per six dice, worse odds the more you roll.

Numbers checked in code (exact binomial sums plus 200,000 simulated rolls of each bet). Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton%E2%80%93Pepys_problem

facts_checked: 1693: Samuel Pepys and Isaac Newton corresponded about the problem; Pepys first thought C (three sixes from 18) most likely, Newton concluded A (one six from 6) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton%E2%80%93Pepys_problem)
A at least 1 six from 6: 0.6651 (67%); B 2 from 12: 0.6187 (62%); C 3 from 18: 0.5973 (60%) (verify.py exact, matches Wikipedia; 200,000 simulated rolls each agree within 0.005)
All 6 dice miss: (5/6)^6 = 33.5%, 'a third of the time' (verify.py)
18 dice: average number of sixes exactly 3; 0, 1 or 2 sixes = 40.3% (4% + 14% + 23%) (verify.py)
Order A > B > C; at least n sixes from 6n dice falls toward one half as n grows (Wikipedia; 10 from 60 = 55%, verify.py)

beats.say: One six from 6 dice, or three from 18: one's the better bet.
It looks like the same bet, one six for every 6 dice. In 1693, Samuel Peeps was sure the 18 dice were better, so he asked Isaac Newton.

beats.say: Newton said no. Check it like he did. With 6 dice, count the misses. Each die misses 5 times in 6, and all six miss a third of the time. So you win 67%.
Now 18 dice. You need three sixes, and on average you roll exactly 3. So why isn't that the safer bet?
Count the ways to fall short. With 6 dice there's only one: no sixes at all. With 18, you fail on zero, one or two. Together, that's 40% of your rolls.
So the 18 dice win just 60%. Two sixes from 12 lands in between, at 62.
67%, then 62, then 60. The same one six per 6 dice, and more dice only make it worse. Peeps had it backwards.
